title: Three transcode tests fail only for the product, not for their own waits, and the two unexplained failures leave a log that can name their cause
description: JS-155's record names three test causes from the queue logs: a hold that catches the lease keeper's first renewal and then swallows its reconnect; a count-based wait that the asset sweep defeats by removing the old track first; a job inserted with no viewer row, which the keeper's cancel can beat to its end (named as likely). Each costs a merge-queue run of about an hour and delays the dogfood's redeploy. Two sightings have no cause because their logs cannot tell. D-043.
acceptanceCriteria: Forced cause 1, a forgotten worker's late renewal: the order is forced by hand, the test's hold landing while the lease keeper's first renewal of the extraction's row has been sent and not yet answered. The unchanged TestAWorkerForgottenWhileItLivesEndsItsExtractionAndItsLateRenewalMovesNoCutLeaseLater fails at its own wait, "a renewal to be on the held keeper connection", and not at any check of the product. The fixed test passes under the same forcing.

Forced cause 2, a sweep between the replace and the wait: the order is forced by hand, an asset sweep by one of the test's own workers removing the replaced file's track after the replace and before the wait. The unchanged TestAfterTheFileIsReplacedAMidFilmRunDrawsAndReadsByTheNewFilesTrack fails at its wait for "the new file's track". The fixed test passes under the same forcing.

Forced cause 3, the keeper's renewal before the job's end: the order is forced by hand, the keeper's first renewal of the job answered before the worker's own end statement. The unchanged TestAJobThatStartsPastTheEndEndsDoneWithNoFFmpeg fails with "ended cancelled, want done". The fixed test ends done under the same forcing.

The sightings of 2026-11-24 are this task's causes: the past-the-end job read cancelled (queue run 45316094444, criterion 3's test) and the asset sweep removing a track before its replacement was stored (run 45339157706, TestTheStoredTrackOfAFileChangedBackIsNeverDeletedByTheSweepThatListedItAnOrphan, with TestTheAssetSweepRemovesAReplacedFilesAndARemovedFilmsTrackAndKeepsACurrentOne, same exposure). For the two sweep tests the old track must still be there, so no worker of the test takes the asset turn before the test's own sweep; the forcing of criterion 2 is shown for them too and they pass after the fix.
If, under criterion 3's forcing, a job that has a viewer still ends cancelled, that is a product finding: it goes to the product owner as a brief and the test is not changed to pass it.

Each forcing in criteria 1 to 4 is done once by hand and not committed (D-069). docs/testing.md records for each: the command and how the order was forced, the failure message before the fix and the result after it, and the machine. A cause that cannot be forced is recorded as cause unknown and goes to the product owner.

After the fix the forgotten-worker test waits for a real renewal: a lease renewal of the extraction's row that the hold kept from Postgres until after the worker was forgotten. Any other statement, or a renewal Postgres had already answered, does not satisfy the wait. A build whose late renewal moves the cut lease later still fails the test.

After the fix the replaced-file test waits for the new file's track: an object in the asset store that it did not hold before the replace, with no extraction queued or running, whether or not the old file's track was swept meanwhile. A build that never stores the new file's track fails at that wait with a message naming it; a build that draws or reads by the old file's track fails the picture or read check.

After the fix the past-the-end job has a viewer of its spec who is not stopped and was seen within the worker's idle time, as every production job has. A build that starts an ffmpeg for the job, fails it, or takes the worker down still fails the test.
For each test in criteria 4 and 7 to 9 the failure on its named wrong build is shown once by hand and its message recorded in docs/testing.md.

The seek-read test's every failure about the film's bytes (TestWithTheTrackStoredASeekIntoALongCueReadsNoMoreOfTheFilmThanAnySeek: a burnt-in seek over its limit; the older cue's seek reading more than the younger's) lists, for each run that read too much, every read of the film in the order opened, with its start offset, the bytes read through it, and the byte position of the cut, so a part read twice shows where it starts. Shown once with a failure forced by hand and recorded.

When an e2e scenario fails, in every gate (browse, play, cors, subtitles, failover, transcode), the run keeps under its log directory (which CI uploads on failure as e2e-logs-<shard>), named by gate and scenario (or gate and step): the viewer's record (every request, answer, socket with its frames, and the timeline, each timed), the browser's whole console at every level plus page errors, and a screenshot taken at the failure.
No failure overwrites another's artifact: two failing scenarios of one gate, the same scenario failing in two E2E_REPEAT iterations, and two failing gates each keep their own files.

In a failed scenario, for every request to the server that the browser reports failed (requestfailed), the output prints its method, path and the browser's error text, and what the test router answered for it: the status and the backend, or that the router received no such request.

A passing scenario keeps no artifact and prints no new line, and a gate whose scenarios all pass takes no longer than before beyond the run-to-run spread (measured once and recorded). The lead may relax this to allow router lines in server.log.

Criteria 12 to 15 are proven by hand: one forced failure in two scenarios of one gate plus a repeat shows the artifacts and the printed line, recorded in docs/testing.md and not committed (the e2e harness is not application behaviour).

No test retries or skips; no wait bound or timeout is raised; the rig's 3 s lease and the forgotten-worker test's 10 s lease are unchanged; no file changes outside *_test.go, test/e2e/ and docs, so no product code is changed to fit a test.

docs/testing.md names this task: the JS-155 table's rows for the three sightings give the forced runs and their verdicts and name JS-160, the 2026-11-24 sightings of criterion 4 name JS-160, and the Historical test failures summary (and its line saying the three were fixed by forcing the order or by the kit's reset keeping live workers) says how they were actually fixed.
No viewer-visible change: no route, response, log line or server behaviour changes.
notes: If the past-the-end check shows the product can end a watched job as cancelled, that is a brief, not a test fix. D-073: starts now beside JS-127, first if the machine holds one. D-058's condition is met: 8 of 8 counted queue runs of PR 270 failed outside the change. The lead confirms whether the asset-sweep and past-the-end sightings of 2026-11-24 are this task's causes.
